items_missed: No agenda statement and no 'sound good?' confirmation — went straight from 'How can I help you today?' into checking availability, so the customer never knew the call had a roadmap or a 10-15 minute shape.
Never asked 'How are you today?' or any rapport opener.
Never used the customer's name once. She introduced herself as Nicole in her first sentence and Jules never said it — zero of the required 3+ name uses.
Never asked about packing services, even though Nicole said outright 'I'm just starting the packing process right now' — that is a live upsell and a live estimate variable, both dropped.
Never asked how many boxes follow-up died — he asked twice, got 'not quite sure,' and left it unresolved with no box-count estimating help (no room-count equivalents, no Ecobox referral).
Never asked about additional stops, storage stops, long walks, narrow hallways, or tight turns.
Never asked 'is there anything you're particularly worried about with this move?' — no stressor probe.

Customer volunteered the garage staging area, the balcony patio furniture, the service elevator, and (at the very end) the three-story stair situation. Jules asked for none of these — he was told them.
No No Worries Damage Coverage pitch — said the word 'insurance' as an included item and never explained the $2,000 coverage or the 60c/lb baseline.

No On-Time Guarantee. This is the biggest single miss: Nicole's whole concern was afternoon timing against a 1:00-4:00 elevator reservation, and Jules told her 'we cannot guarantee exactly the time we would be arriving' without ever giving her the discount-if-we-miss-the-window backstop.

Clock explanation almost entirely absent — the 2.5 hour minimum only appeared buried inside the time range; no 'clock starts on-site when the contract opens,' no 15-minute prorated increments, no sense-check.

Entire Save Your Ass prep speech missing — no 'prep before move day means a shorter move and a lower bill,' no consolidation examples, no 'take a carload' tip. On a move where the customer is mid-pack with an unknown box count, this was the highest-value 90 seconds available and it never happened.

Estimate variables not explained: three stories of stairs at origin plus a 6th-floor elevator destination were never named as time drivers, nor was walk distance from the back garage, nor packing time, nor disassembly/reassembly time for the bed, desk and dresser.
2.5-4.5 hours for a 3-story origin, a 6th-floor elevator destination, patio furniture and an unknown box count is an optimistic top end with no hedge language.
Never asked 'any other questions before I let you go?'
Never gave office hours or how to reach us.
Talked over the customer during the item list — cut in with 'Patio furniture. Okay, do you happen to have like an idea? Okay.' while she was still describing bathroom and balcony items.
top_strength: Jules solved the customer's real constraint without being asked to. Nicole had a service elevator locked from 1:00 to 4:00 and was worried the arrival window wouldn't fit; Jules proactively offered 'we can do a start time of around like 11:30 to 1:30 so we can arrive earlier at your current townhome' so the 1:00 elevator slot would work. He was also honest and upfront about the afternoon window limitation rather than overpromising a hard time. The no-hidden-fees pitch was clean and specific — gas, truck, taxes, insurance, tools, blankets, no fuel fee, no assembly fee — and he handled the 'is two movers enough?' objection directly. Booked the job in under seven minutes.
coaching_note: Jules, the single highest-leverage fix is the On-Time Guarantee, and you had the perfect setup for it. The moment you told Nicole 'we cannot guarantee exactly the time we would be arriving,' you needed the next sentence to be: 'That said, we back it up — if we miss your window, we start discounting your move immediately, so the risk is on us, not on your elevator reservation.' You left her holding the uncertainty when we have a differentiator built exactly for that. Second priority: run the Save Your Ass speech every single time, and this call was the textbook case — she told you she was just starting to pack and couldn't count her boxes, which is your cue for 'here's how you shave time off your bill: consolidate the loose stuff into boxes, get the photos off the walls, and take a carload of the small things yourself. Does that make sense?' Third, use her name. She gave you 'Nicole' in her opening line and you never said it once in six and a half minutes — that costs you politeness points and it costs you the feeling of a real conversation. Last thing: you stopped probing the second you had enough to price. Packing services, additional stops, and 'anything you're particularly worried about?' each take ten seconds and each one is either revenue or estimate accuracy. You closed the sale — now close it with the full pitch.
phone_presence_notes: Consistently polite with light affirmations ('No problem,' 'Sounds good,' 'Awesome,' 'it's my pleasure') and the customer stayed positive throughout, but the call was transactional — zero name use, no empathy or stress-acknowledgment language, no rapport moment, and one instance of talking over her mid-answer.
